column1: # async_check.py allowlist. Columns (tab separated): file, rule, anchor regex, class, count, note.
# allow: cheap or off-reactor, with the reason. owed: the decision or step that removes it. compiled_out: the switch.

column6: dump_documents(fd) and restore_documents(fd) serve the CLI --dump and --restore on the main thread (check_may_block guards it)
a RESTORE's placement and apply children take one shard's turn each under engine::counted; the lock_shard itself takes no turn (x7-loop-fix-c)
a lock_shard registers a use of the entry and takes no turn: every database call of the handler is an awaited task, and the operation takes the turn (D5)
the log is read in a query chore of repr_wal, never on a reactor thread

a RESTORE's prepare chore runs Schema::index on a WorkPool worker (inline on the CLI's main thread); CPU only there: scripts are barriers and seq is never 0, so no call_script or lock_shard (x7-loop-stalls)
the list of live IndexChores: O(1) link and unlink; cancel_all walks it at shutdown on the main thread, after the loops stopped (task D8)
the catalog timer's pending callbacks: O(1) sections that add, take or swap out an entry, none with I/O; the callbacks run outside it and only post (D58)
std::weak_ptr::lock in the catalog timer's callback, not a mutex: it takes no lock (D58)
the shutdown's state: O(1) sections that set or read its flag and the keys whose commit failed, none with I/O (x-pool D10)
join() and ~DatabasePool await the catalog's shutdown on the main thread after the loops stopped; join is guarded by check_may_block (x-pool D10, C24)
the catalog's resolve runs in its open chore on a WorkPool worker: it checks and makes the index directory there (x-pool D6)
IndexChores::cancel_all polls the groups at shutdown on the main thread, after the loops stopped (task D8)
a detached task with no control loop runs to its end on the thread that started it (a timer thread, the CLI); guarded by check_may_block
the entry's O(1) state lock, for the uuid (D5)
the declaration: the blob fsync runs as a flush chore (D7)
Schema::index awaits the shard it counts; a lock_shard pins the index (x-pool D3) and takes no turn (D5)

LRU map lookup, insert and trim under the lock; compare_schema is bounded by one schema (D11); the flights' loads publish into it and their probes read it, O(1) sections with no I/O, taken and released before any await
the entry: O(1) state sections under its mutex, and the turn, an async mutex a task awaits without blocking; the catalog's commit chore tries it with no pin held (D5, x-pool D7)
the blob commit runs in a flush chore, first in the commit chore (D7)
the definition: the commit is chores_.run(flush, ...) (D7)
the blob writes, reads and rollovers run in flush chores of the entry or the upload (D9)
a RESTORE's apply slice writes in a flush chore on a WorkPool worker, in the index's turn with the engine's chores inline: chore code, never a request thread (x7-loop-fix-c)
the open chore reads the id counter on a WorkPool worker before the replay: strata's metadata() finds the key in the open view's map and never suspends, no I/O (one-id)
the open chore replays the WAL and opens the engine on a WorkPool worker, with chores inline (D4, D8): chore code, never a request thread
the open chore replays the log on a WorkPool worker (D4, D8)
ENGINE_CENSUS is OFF in gate builds (D1)
ENGINE_CENSUS is OFF in gate builds (D1)
BlockingScheduler: its queue (resumes and post_call functions) and timers under one mutex, each O(1); the thread that drives it may block by definition (check_may_block guards engine::sync_wait)
BlockingScheduler::drive waits for a resume or a timer on the thread that called engine::sync_wait; guarded by check_may_block
SleepFor suspends the task on its host's timer; a task that runs on no host (a test, the CLI) sleeps its own thread, never a loop's
NDEBUG: Counted exists only in debug builds, where a request's queued resumes sit under one mutex in O(1) sections (push, swap, empty check)
acquire runs only in a query chore (open_local, check): opening the core reads the directory there, never on a reactor (D4); borrow only names the directory, in the catalog's open chore (x-pool D2)
the entry lock: acquire holds it across the open I/O inside a chore, only while no handle exists, so no ~Handle can contend for it; ~Handle takes it for an O(1) count (D4, D5)
drain_readers suspends the closing task between polls for the readers of the old index (D6); it holds no thread
map lookup and insert of the open-core registry: O(log n) under the lock, no I/O (D1)
check_may_block's own diagnostics lock, taken only when a guard trips
the bridge itself; every call is guarded by check_may_block (D14)
the directory walk of a pattern runs in a query chore of the work pool (expand_paths), never on a reactor thread

the settings map: O(log n) lookups and inserts under the lock, released before a settings read and taken again after it (D11); the flight's store and its probe are such sections too (the probe copies the shards under the lock: O(shards))
fd serialisers used only by --dump and --restore on the CLI main thread
weak_ptr promotion, not a mutex
process startup, signal handlers and the CLI --dump and --restore, before or beside the loops and never on a reactor
the CLI --dump, --restore and resolve wait on the main thread (check_may_block guards it)
CLI main thread waits for the node to settle (check_may_block guards it)
the node-name file is read and written once by run() on the main thread, before the loop and the listeners exist
the signal self-pipe: nonblocking descriptor setup and one-byte writes
an atomic flag, not I/O
setsockopt on an accepted socket: one syscall, no wait
the node map under _nodes_mtx: lookup and insert, O(log n)
preload_mime_types reads mime.types at startup, before the listeners open; mime_type reads the loaded table (D1)
wal_view awaits the chore that reads the log
preloadStopWords reads the stop word files at startup, before the listeners open; getStopWords reads the loaded table (D1)
stat of --tls-key while the TLS context is built, before the listeners open
runs on the FS debouncer thread (D8, until 7b), never on a reactor
Storage IO policy wrappers; their callers are chores (D9) or the WL thread (D8)
the volume of an aborted upload is removed in a flush chore (D9)
the walk for Xapian files runs on the main thread at startup, before the listeners open (D1)
published_position() spins for a writer that stores two words; nothing in Xapiand, strata or prospect calls it (grep): the callers use try_published_position() (D1)
storage admission only: Xapiand sets no storage permit and options::defer_io, so apply answers drain_owed and this site is not reached (D6)
storage admission only: Xapiand sets no storage permit and options::defer_io, so apply answers drain_owed and this site is not reached (D6)
the shutdown checks after the control loop ended run on the main thread; check_may_block guards it (D13)
the control tasks' state (a wake pointer, cleared by a scope guard, a key's target, one map entry): O(1) sections, never held across a wait or a call (D13)
the state shared with the thread that runs a blocking stop: a flag under a lock, on the main thread at shutdown; check_may_block guards the entry (D14)
the shutdown's bounded wait for a blocking stop (C14), on the main thread; check_may_block guards it (D14)
the flights map: one lookup or erase under the lock, never held across the load or a wait (D11)
